{
"Service-Oriented Architecture": "An architectural style that structures software systems as collections of loosely coupled, independently deployable services that communicate through well-defined contracts. It promotes reusability, interoperability, and flexibility in building distributed enterprise systems.",
"Service": "A self-contained, independently deployable software unit that exposes specific functionality through a defined contract and interface. Services are the fundamental building blocks of a Service-Oriented Architecture.",
"Contract": "A formal specification that defines the obligations, behavior, inputs, outputs, and constraints of a service. It establishes the agreement between a service provider and its consumers.",
"Interface": "The technical boundary through which a service exposes its operations and can be invoked by consumers. It specifies the methods, parameters, and protocols used for interaction.",
"Functionality": "The specific set of capabilities, operations, or business logic that a service provides to its consumers. It represents what the service actually does when invoked.",
"Composition": "The process of combining multiple services together to create higher-level functionality or fulfill complex business requirements. It enables the construction of larger solutions from reusable service components.",
"Business Process": "A structured sequence of activities and tasks performed by an organization to achieve a specific business goal or outcome. In SOA, business processes are often realized through the composition and orchestration of services.",
"Orchestration": "The coordinated execution and management of multiple services according to a defined workflow to accomplish a business process. It involves a central coordinator that controls the sequence and logic of service invocations.",
"Workflow": "A defined sequence of steps, tasks, or service invocations that describes how a process should be executed. It specifies the order, conditions, and data flow between activities.",
"Governance": "The set of policies, standards, processes, and controls applied to manage the lifecycle, quality, and compliance of services within an SOA. It ensures consistency, accountability, and alignment with organizational objectives.",
"Service Versioning": "The practice of managing and tracking different versions of a service's contract and implementation over time. It enables evolution and change while maintaining backward compatibility for existing consumers.",
"Quality": "The degree to which services meet functional and non-functional requirements such as reliability, performance, security, and maintainability. It is a key concern of governance in service-oriented systems.",
"Loose Coupling": "A design principle in which services have minimal dependencies on one another, interacting only through well-defined contracts. This allows services to evolve, scale, and fail independently without impacting others.",
"Independent Deployability": "The property that allows a service to be built, deployed, updated, and scaled without requiring changes or redeployment of other services. It is enabled by loose coupling and stable service contracts.",
"System": "A collection of interrelated components, including services, infrastructure, and processes, that work together to deliver business or technical capabilities. In SOA, a system is typically realized as an assembly of composed services."
}
